title: Stanford from St. Asaph
summary: Benjamin Logan planted St. Asaph at Buffalo Spring in 1775, his fort held through a 1777 siege, and the county seat built there was named Stanford in 1786.
bodyMarkdown:
[Stanford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford,_Kentucky) began in 1775 as St. Asaph, also called Logan's Fort. [Benjamin Logan](/stories/benjamin-logan/) [left Richard Henderson's party at Hazel Patch](https://history.ky.gov/markers/logans-station) and headed for the spot. He [left Boone's Road on April 15, 1775](https://history.ky.gov/markers/wilderness-roadlogans-station), and the station dates from May 1, 1775.

## Building the fort

Logan came with [John Floyd](/stories/john-floyd/) and settled near Buffalo Spring on Skagg's Trace. The [stockade measured about 150 by 90 feet](https://explorekyhistory.ky.gov/items/show/572) and enclosed family cabins. The settlement also sent representatives to the Transylvania government at Boonesborough. The fort site lay about a mile west of today's courthouse, and the town's main street follows an old buffalo trail.

## The 1777 siege

The Revolutionary War reached the Kentucky stations in 1777. In May of that year Native warriors allied with the British besieged Logan's Fort for 13 days. During the siege, Logan rescued the wounded Burr Harrison, carrying him to safety behind a feather mattress. The fort held, and the stand gave Logan's Fort its lasting reputation.

## A county seat

Lincoln County was one of Kentucky's three original counties. In 1781 Logan donated land for a courthouse at the new town. One account says the county court met at Fort Harrod until 1785.

The town was chartered by 1786, and a log courthouse opened in 1787. [Another account](https://grokipedia.com/page/Stanford,_Kentucky) dates the log courthouse to 1786.

The county's records have never been lost to fire or flood. They are complete from November 1789 and include deeds signed by Daniel Boone and Simon Kenton. A Presbyterian church followed in 1790, on land donated by Logan's sister, Mary Briggs.

## The name

The name Stanford came into use around 1790. One account traces it to "Standing Fort," a nickname earned when Logan's Fort withstood attack. Another suggests it came from Stamford, England.

## Kentucky today

Stanford remains the seat of Lincoln County. It is often counted as Kentucky's second-oldest permanent settlement. The town lies along the old Wilderness Road corridor that carried migrants west through the Cumberland Gap. The nearby [William Whitley House](/stories/william-whitley-sportsmans-hill/), built in 1788, is called the oldest brick house in Kentucky. In 2025 Stanford marked its 250th anniversary with a weeklong celebration of its founding.
